title: Dividing Fractions
subtitle: Fractions · Mission 01
tagline: Learn the {{cyan:keep–change–flip}} move — and find out {{amber:why it actually works}}.

slides.headline: You've got {{cyan:½ of a pizza}} left. You want to split it into {{amber:3 equal pieces}}. How much pizza is one piece?
body: You already know the answer is small. Way smaller than half. Each piece is a slice *of* a half — one-sixth of the whole pizza.
That's {{cyan:½ ÷ 3}}. Dividing a fraction by a whole number. And here's the wild part: the fastest way to solve it doesn't look like division at all. It looks like *multiplication*.
Today's power-up: **keep–change–flip.** By the end of this mission, you'll know the move *and* the reason it works — so you can never be tricked into forgetting it.

slides.definition: The reciprocal of a fraction is the same fraction {{cyan:flipped upside down}}.
slides.plainWords: Swap the top and the bottom.
slides.analogy: Think of it like a **power-up in a video game**. The number `¾` walks up to a mirror, and the mirror hands it back as `⁴⁄₃`. Same digits — different roles. `3` used to be the top; now it's the bottom. Every fraction has a reciprocal, and every reciprocal has a reciprocal (it flips back).

slides.pronunciation: the three parts of any division problem
slides.definition: In `A ÷ B = C`, `A` is the {{cyan:dividend}}, `B` is the {{amber:divisor}}, and `C` is the answer — the {{cyan:quotient}}.
slides.plainWords: The first number is what you're splitting up. The second number is what you're splitting it into. The answer is what each piece looks like.
slides.analogy: **Loot-drop analogy:** the `dividend` is the pile of loot you just picked up. The `divisor` is how many teammates you're sharing with. The `quotient` is what each teammate walks away with.

slides.headline: Keep–Change–Flip: three tiny moves, one big power-up
slides.intro: Every fraction-division problem gets solved with the same three-step combo. Memorize the combo, then we'll break down why it works.

cards.name: KEEP
cards.description: **Keep** the first fraction exactly the way it is. Don't touch it. Copy it down.

cards.name: CHANGE
cards.description: **Change** the `÷` sign to a `×` sign. Division becomes multiplication.

cards.name: FLIP
cards.description: **Flip** the second fraction to its `reciprocal` — swap the top and bottom.

slides.headline: Dividing by a fraction = multiplying by its reciprocal
slides.intro: This isn't a trick. It's the actual rule. Here's the reason in plain language:

cards.name: DIVISION ASKS "HOW MANY FITS?"
cards.description: `6 ÷ 2` asks: **how many 2's fit inside 6?** Answer: three. So `6 ÷ ½` asks: **how many halves fit inside 6?** Answer: {{cyan:twelve}} — because every whole thing has *two* halves.

cards.name: DIVIDING BY A SMALL NUMBER MAKES THE ANSWER BIGGER
cards.description: This is the part that feels weird. When you divide `6` by `½`, you don't get `3`. You get `12`. That's why the flip works — flipping `½` gives you `2`, and `6 × 2 = 12`. The math checks out.

cards.name: SO WHEN YOU FLIP, YOU'RE ASKING THE SAME QUESTION IN AN EASIER FORM
cards.description: `⅔ ÷ ¾` and `⅔ × ⁴⁄₃` have the exact same answer. The flipped version is just the version your calculator can handle in one shot.

slides.headline: How to solve any fraction ÷ fraction problem
slides.intro: Do these three moves, in this order, every single time. No skipping. No shortcuts.

rows.name: Step 1 — Write down the first fraction
rows.description: Copy the {{cyan:dividend}} exactly as it appears. Don't simplify yet, don't flip it, don't touch it.

rows.name: Step 2 — Flip the `÷` to a `×`
rows.description: The division sign is the trigger. Change it to a multiplication sign so you can use the multiply move you already know.

rows.name: Step 3 — Flip the second fraction
rows.description: The {{cyan:divisor}} becomes its `reciprocal`. Top and bottom swap. This is the whole magic of the move.

counter.label: COMMON TRAP
counter.text: Do NOT flip the first fraction. Only the second one flips. Ever.

rows.name: Step 4 — Multiply straight across
rows.description: New top = top × top. New bottom = bottom × bottom. Then simplify if you can.

correct.title: ✓ FLIPPED IT
body: Top and bottom swapped. `⅖` → `⁵⁄₂`. That's the reciprocal, every time.
correct.followup: **Pro move:** whenever you see the word `reciprocal`, your hand should already be flipping the fraction — no thinking required.

a.title: ✕ NOT QUITE — THAT'S THE SAME FRACTION
body: You copied `⅖` back down. A reciprocal has to **flip**. Swap the top and the bottom.

c.title: ✕ CLOSE — BUT NEGATIVE ISN'T THE MOVE
body: Reciprocals aren't about **signs** (positive/negative). They're about **positions** (top/bottom). `⅖` flipped is `⁵⁄₂`, and it stays positive.

d.title: ✕ MISFIRE — WHERE DID THAT 7 COME FROM?
body: A reciprocal only uses the digits *already in the fraction*. `⅖` has a `2` and a `5`. The reciprocal is `⁵⁄₂` — same digits, swapped.

prompt.label: TACTICAL DRILL
prompt.scenario: You need to solve `¾ ÷ ⅖`. Put the four steps in the correct order.
prompt.question: Drag the moves into the right sequence.

items.text: Multiply straight across: top × top, bottom × bottom.
Keep the first fraction (`¾`) exactly as it is.
Change the `÷` sign to a `×` sign.

correct.title: ✓ COMBO EXECUTED
body: Keep. Change. Flip. Multiply. That's the whole move, in order. This is the combo you'll use for every fraction-division problem from here on.
correct.followup: **Memory trick:** say it out loud when you're solving — "keep, change, flip" — until your hand does it automatically.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ ALMOST — ONE STEP IS OUT OF PLACE
body: The order is: **① Keep** the first fraction, **② Change** the sign, **③ Flip** the second fraction, **④ Multiply** across. If you flip before you change the sign, or multiply before you flip, you'll get a wrong answer.

prompt.label: LOOT SORT
prompt.scenario: Each division problem below has a matching flipped-multiplication version. Pair them up.
prompt.question: Match each problem on the left to the correct rewritten version on the right.

correct.title: ✓ ALL PAIRS LOCKED
body: You spotted the pattern: the first fraction stays exactly the same, the sign changes, and the *second* fraction flips. Every time.
correct.followup: **Pro move:** when you're not sure which fraction to flip, remember — the first one never moves. Only the divisor flips.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ ONE OR MORE PAIRS ARE OFF
body: Check each pair one at a time. In every correct pair, the **first fraction is untouched** and the **second fraction is flipped** (top and bottom swapped).

prompt.label: BOSS-ROOM WARM-UP
prompt.scenario: Solve: `½ ÷ ¾`. Show your work by filling in each blank.
prompt.question: Fill in the missing pieces of the keep–change–flip solution.

blanks.hint: The reciprocal of ¾ has this number on top.
The reciprocal of ¾ has this number on bottom.

correct.title: ✓ SOLVED
body: `½ ÷ ¾ = ⁴⁄₆`, which simplifies to `⅔`. You flipped the divisor, multiplied across, and got the answer. That's the whole game.
correct.followup: **Next level:** try `⁴⁄₆` in your head — is that already simplified? Both 4 and 6 divide by 2, so `⁴⁄₆` = `⅔`. Simplifying is a separate move, and you'll get faster with practice.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ CHECK YOUR FLIP
body: The reciprocal of `¾` is `⁴⁄₃` — the `4` goes on top, the `3` goes on bottom. Then multiply straight across: `1 × 4 = 4` on top, `2 × 3 = 6` on bottom. Answer: `⁴⁄₆` (or `⅔` simplified).

prompt.label: CONCEPT CHECK
prompt.scenario: Your friend says: "I hate keep–change–flip. It's just a random trick. Why does flipping the second fraction even work?"
prompt.question: Which explanation is the best answer?

options.text: It's not a trick — dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. Flipping just rewrites the problem in a form you can actually calculate.
It works because fractions are hard, and flipping makes them easier to look at.
It works because the ÷ sign has a top dot and a bottom dot, so you flip.
It's a rule your teacher made up so tests would be easier to grade.

correct.title: ✓ LOCKED IN
body: That's the real answer. `÷ B` and `× (1/B)` mean the exact same thing. Flipping the second fraction turns division into multiplication — same question, easier form.
correct.followup: **Pro move:** when someone tells you a math rule feels random, there's almost always a reason underneath it. Ask *why* until you find the reason. Then it stops being a trick and starts being knowledge.

b.title: ✕ NOT QUITE — THERE'S A REAL REASON
body: Flipping isn't just for convenience. It's a **mathematical identity** — dividing by a number and multiplying by its reciprocal give the exact same answer, always. That's why it works.

c.title: ✕ FUN GUESS, BUT NO
body: The `÷` symbol having dots is a coincidence. The reason flipping works is that division and multiplication-by-reciprocal are literally the same operation.

d.title: ✕ TEACHERS DIDN'T INVENT THIS ONE
body: This rule comes from how fractions and division work — not from a grading convenience. It's been true for centuries.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ RECALIBRATE
body: The reason keep–change–flip works: dividing by any number is the same thing as multiplying by its reciprocal. Flipping is what turns a division problem into a multiplication problem you already know how to solve.

slides.headline: MISSION COMPLETE
slides.subtext: You've got keep–change–flip. Fraction division is unlocked.
